newsitem.title: USA: U.S. money managers stay bullish on US debt -- MCM.
newsitem.headline: U.S. money managers stay bullish on US debt -- MCM.

text.p: U.S. fixed-income managers aggressively extended the durations of their U.S. debt portfolios over the past week, according to an MCM MoneyWatch Inc survey.
"Cash was put to work as indicated by the drop in cash levels," said MCM first vice president and economist Astrid Adolfson, who released the survey.
The survey showed durations as a percentage of benchmark rose to 108.0 percent in the week ending May 5 from 106.5 in the prior week.
A duration reading above 100 percent indicates the group of investors polled is mostly long on the market.
A portfolio's duration represents its average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
In the "next likely move" category, portfolio managers representing 33 percent of total assets in the survey said they would "buy," compared with 43 percent the prior week.
Strategists leaning toward "sell" rose to 10 percent, up from 6.0 percent the week ended April 28.
Fifty-seven percent of managers said they were "neutral" on the market, up from 51 percent a week ago.
Cash as a percentage of assets fell to 3.06 percent, against 3.24 percent registered the previous week.

The survey showed 35 percent of investors polled overweighted the 10-plus years duration sector, unchanged from the previous week, while 9.0 percent underweighted it. The remaining 56 percent were "neutral."
In the five- to 10-year duration sector, 40 percent of investors polled said they overweighted the securities and 19 percent underweighted them.
The survey included 38 domestic participants who manage about $110 billion in fixed-income assets. The poll is conducted weekly by MCM and usually is released on Tuesday.
